title: Hard bounds
body:
This PR adresses that specifying bounds for the FOURIER coefficient does not really make sense.
Instead, now, when applying bounds with the FOURIER strategy, hard limits for beta and gamma parameters are set after applying the sine and cosine transformations.
Resulting parameters are in $\beta \in [-\pi / 2, \pi / 2]^p$ and $\gamma \in [0, \pi ]^p$.
If a $\gamma$ parameters is negative, we account for the QAOA symmetries, by flipping the sign of the respective gamma and beta parameter. 

**Example**:
If the $v$ and $u$ parameters result in a gamma parameter of $\gamma_1=-5$, and a beta parameter of $\beta_1=1$ applying the bound results in $\gamma_{1,b}=\pi$ and $\beta_{1, b} = -1$, through flipping and applying bounds.

Additionally, parameters are also normalised according to bounds and symmetries, when computing the annealing schedules from the parameters.

title: Random perturbation for FOURIER strategy
body: This PR implements the random perturbations for the FOURIER strategy, described by [Zhou et al.](https://journals.aps.org/prx/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevX.10.021067), appendix B2.

title: Reproducible QUBOs
body:
This PR addressed #38 by making sure that the QUBO remains the same, when testing the same configuration multiple times.
- Serialisation now directly uses the export function of the trackrec model.
- Export of xplets was removed as not needed
- Even more important: There was a bug in the QUBO->Ising function when determining the linear terms. This is fixed now. Note that we have a fundamentally different Hamiltonian now!
- Quadratic terms of the QUBO are balanced now, instead of having the term just in one half of the Ising matrix, which should actually not make a difference.

title: Parameter Initialisation Strategies
body:
This PR adds the following initialisation strategies as an option:
- "first_random": For p=1, initialise beta and gamma randomly, for p>1 take parameter from p-1 and pad with zeros  
- "random": For p=1, initialise beta and gamma randomly, for p>1 take parameter from p-1 and pad with random values
- "all_zeros": Initialise all parameters with zeros, without re-using parameters from p-1
- "all_random": Initialise all parameters randomly, without re-using parameters from p-1

The last two options are probably not really of interest.

This addresses #32 and depends on #31.

title: Composed dataset
body:
This PR introduces a composed dataset that can be used in the catalog in conjunction with an arbitrary other dataset e.g.:
```
composed_dataset_name
  type: fromhopetoheuristics.datasets.composed_dataset.ComposedDataset
  filepath: data/00_test/foo.bar
  versioned: true
  dataset:
    type: kedro.FooBarDataset
    resolver: foo_bar_dataset
```
This will create a versioned dataset of type `FooBarDataset` which, due to the wrapping `ComposedDataset` has the ability to handle a dynamic number of actual output files.
This works by taking a dictionary from the generating node as input and using its keys as filenames and the value for saving with underlying (`FooBarDataset`) instance.
E.g. one could have the following dictionary as node output:
```python
{
    "0": FooBarObject,
    "1": FooBarObject
}
```
which would result in the following IO:
```
data/00_test/foo/VERSION/0.bar
data/00_test/foo/VERSION/1.bar
```
Note that the dataset name ("foo") and extension ("bar") are being inferred from the `filepath` property as defined in the catalog.
Note also that currently we require an ugly `resolver` property, which is because of the way Kedro imports datasets (and I'm not smart enough to deal with it).

title: Catalog
body:
This PR resolves #11 by
- moving IO interaction to kedro by introducing various datasets in the catalog
- removing file actions in various nodes and pipelines
  - [x] adiabatic maxcut
  - [x] adiabatic trackrec
  - [x] anneal schedule
  - [x] generation
  - [x] qaoa maxcut
  - [x] qaoa trackrec
  - [x] qubo
  - [x] visualization
- cleaning up variable dependencies
- copied the sample events into `01_raw` (persistent in git now). In the long run we should utilize e.g. the trackml library to load arbitrary event data (e.g. based on a parameter)
- added `cleanup.sh` to remove any data that nodes created
- [ ] update docstring (once concept is approved by @majafranz )

**Note1**: ~~When merging from main, I broke the `geometric_index` stuff, because of conflicts. Should be fixed before merging back again.~~ Fixed it, parameter is now considered when building qubo.
**Note2**: I added a mean value calc. in the anneal schedules method, because the length of the vectors did not add up. However, I might have messed sth. up with the datatype when saving, so please check that.
**Note3**: The visualization pipeline is only roughly implemented and lacks more details, but we should discuss that in a meeting how to proceed imo. Because the "approach" slightly changed with this PR from "put all in one CSV and have parameters embedded there" to "separate result files and parameters are being inferred from the config", context is always required when visualizing from the result files. One quick-and-dirty solution would be to have a final "collection" node that gathers together all the results and required parameter and then builds up the `solution.csv` file which is being used for plotting right now. A much cleaner solution would be the plotting of the individual results directly as kedro node, which, however, would require switching from R to Python or using the `ggplot2` port.
**Note4**: In the long run we could utilize namespaces to allow switching between track-reconstruction and maxcut and thus reusing existing nodes to be a bit closer to the "spirit"
